messages.subject: Re: Job fails when running on cluster
messages.subject_clean: Job fails when running on cluster
messages.body_plain:
Ahhh.  I was just coming to post about a very similar looking problem
with a cluster I been trying to setup.  I  been stalling for a couple
weeks on fixing that same sort of output.  I was lost for what I
should work.  I should have asked sooner.

Mine was:

Script:

a = list()
a$ofolder =  "/jrounds/tmp/lapply"
a$inout = c("lapply", "sequence")
a$jobname = a$ofolder
a$N = 10

a$map = expression({
    for(i in seq_along(map.values)){
        rhcollect(1,runif(1000))
    }

})

mr = do.call("rhmr",a)
ex = rhex(mr)

In case the original poster is interested, my problem was fixed by
using the following runner command.  You may be able to mimic it by
doing a locate imperious.so on your system.

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()
rhoptions(runner =  "R CMD /ln/cluster_node_image/R/lib64/R/library/
Rhipe/libs/imperious.so --slave --silent --vanilla --max-ppsize=100000
--max-nsize=1G")

a = list()
a$ofolder =  "/jrounds/tmp/lapply"
a$inout = c("lapply", "sequence")
a$jobname = a$ofolder

a$N = 2

a$map = expression({
    for(i in seq_along(map.values)){
        rhcollect(1,runif(1000))
    }

})

mr = do.call("rhmr",a)
ex = rhex(mr)

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Roadmap of RHipe
messages.subject_clean: [rhipe] Roadmap of RHipe
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

So, there isn't too much to extend.

a) A protocol buffer based sequence file format, so it can be read
from other languages.
b) better debugging support
c) Maybe extra addons e.g. regression on RHIPE, see
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE-Additions
d) improvements to reducer when millions of keys each with a few set
of values (in this cass more time is spent on parsing/setting up
context for the expression than any useful work)
e) tutorials/papers.
f) Possibly, automatically ave the calling environment, so that the
map/reducer code automatically can access the functions declared
outside (only persist objects less than X bytes large or place a cap
on total size of persisted objects)

Do you or anybody else have suggestions for improvements?

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Running and setup woes
messages.subject_clean: Running and setup woes
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Having seen the woes involved in running Rhipe, i strongly recommend
the approach discussed
at http://code.google.com/p/rhipe/wiki/RHIPEonNodesWithoutR .

I use it everyday and the setup cost is rather painless. The trickiest
bit is the script and the issues involved .
Using this approach, users can have custom R distributions across
nodes. User A can have library L1 and User B can have library L2.
Updating this to include new libaries could be automated too.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Well did you checked whether the dependencies on imperious.so is fine or not? i faced it and when i did
ldd imperious.so (full path to imperious.so)i found that libR.so was not found, i put it in the LD_LIBRARY_PATH and it worked fine.

Moreover you can try giving the location of imperious.so in the rhoptions function.

Regards,
Som

messages.body_plain:
Okay I read up on sed and parsed the script in my head.

My understanding is you don't actually need an install in home
directories you are just using that script named "R" as a generic
script to edit via sed and put in the new install, and it so happens
you know there is that script named "R" at a certain spot in your home
directory.

 If that is the case then I think the proper thing to do is carry that
script named "R" with the install in the tar.gz and also replace what
would be the /home/sguha/lib64 with something generic like LIB64PATH
and then have sed operate on that script for making a copy.

I don't have the luxury of a common home directory at every node, but
with those changes this plan should work.

My R script btw looks like what follows.  Under the plan I will change
"/ln/cluster_node_image/R/lib64" to "LIB64PATH" copy this with the
tar.gz.  Then change the sed line to: sed   "s;LIB64PATH\/;${bin}\/;g"
genericRrunner > $Rex

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#!/bin/sh
# Shell wrapper for R executable.

R_HOME_DIR=/ln/cluster_node_image/R/lib64/R
if test "${R_HOME_DIR}" = "/ln/cluster_node_image/R/lib64/R"; then
   case "linux-gnu" in
   linux*)
     run_arch=`uname -m`
     case "$run_arch" in
        x86_64|mips64|ppc64|powerpc64|sparc64|s390x)
          libnn=lib64
          libnn_fallback=lib
        ;;
        *)
          libnn=lib
          libnn_fallback=lib64
        ;;
     esac
     if [ -x "/ln/cluster_node_image/R/${libnn}/R/bin/exec/R" ]; then
        R_HOME_DIR="/ln/cluster_node_image/R/${libnn}/R"
     elif [ -x "/ln/cluster_node_image/R/${libnn_fallback}/R/bin/exec/
R" ]; then
        R_HOME_DIR="/ln/cluster_node_image/R/${libnn_fallback}/R"
     ## else -- leave alone (might be a sub-arch)
     fi
     ;;
  esac
fi

if test -n "${R_HOME}" && \
   test "${R_HOME}" != "${R_HOME_DIR}"; then
  echo "WARNING: ignoring environment value of R_HOME"
fi
R_HOME="${R_HOME_DIR}"
export R_HOME
R_SHARE_DIR=/ln/cluster_node_image/R/lib64/R/share
export R_SHARE_DIR
R_INCLUDE_DIR=/ln/cluster_node_image/R/lib64/R/include
export R_INCLUDE_DIR
R_DOC_DIR=/ln/cluster_node_image/R/lib64/R/doc
export R_DOC_DIR

# Since this script can be called recursively, we allow R_ARCH to
# be overridden from the environment.
# This script is shared by parallel installs, so nothing in it should
# depend on the sub-architecture except the default here.
: ${R_ARCH=}

usage="
Usage: R [options] [< infile] [> outfile]
   or: R CMD command [arguments]

Start R, a system for statistical computation and graphics, with the
specified options, or invoke an R tool via the 'R CMD' interface.

Options:
  -h, --help            Print short help message and exit
  --version             Print version info and exit
  --encoding=ENC        Specify encoding to be used for stdin
  --encoding ENC
  RHOME			Print path to R home directory and exit
  --save                Do save workspace at the end of the session
  --no-save             Don't save it
  --no-environ          Don't read the site and user environment files
  --no-site-file        Don't read the site-wide Rprofile
  --no-init-file        Don't read the user R profile
  --restore             Do restore previously saved objects at startup
  --no-restore-data     Don't restore previously saved objects
  --no-restore-history  Don't restore the R history file
  --no-restore          Don't restore anything
  --vanilla		Combine --no-save, --no-restore, --no-site-file,
			--no-init-file and --no-environ
  --no-readline         Don't use readline for command-line editing
  --min-vsize=N         Set vector heap min to N bytes; '4M' = 4 MegaB
  --max-vsize=N         Set vector heap max to N bytes;
  --min-nsize=N         Set min number of cons cells to N
  --max-nsize=N         Set max number of cons cells to N
  --max-ppsize=N        Set max size of protect stack to N
  -q, --quiet           Don't print startup message
  --silent              Same as --quiet
  --slave               Make R run as quietly as possible
  --interactive         Force an interactive session

### Argument loop

debugger=
debugger_args=
gui=
while test -n "${1}"; do

      export R_ARCH
      . "${R_HOME}/etc${R_ARCH}/ldpaths"
      exec sh "${R_HOME}/bin/Rcmd" "${@}" ;;

	gui="${2}"
        args="${args} ${1} ${2}"
	shift
      else
	error "option '${1}' requires an argument"
      fi
      ;;
    --gui=*)

      args="${args} ${1}"
      ;;
    -d|--debugger)

	debugger="${2}"; shift
      else
	error "option '${1}' requires an argument"
      fi

      args="${args} ${1}"

      args="${args} ${1}"
      ;;

      export R_ENVIRON_USER=''
      export R_PROFILE=''
      export R_PROFILE_USER=''
      args="${args} ${1}"

      args="${args} ${1}" ;;

Tk|tk|X11|x11)

"")
  ;;

know

  ## command line args.
  args_ok=no

          grep ' *--args' >/dev/null; then
	args_ok=yes
	debugger_args="${debugger_args} --args"
      fi
      ;;
    valgrind*)
      args_ok=yes
      ;;
  esac

    echo "*** (maybe use 'run ${args}' from *inside* ${debugger})"

messages.subject: reading rhipe data outside of hadoop
messages.subject_clean: reading rhipe data outside of hadoop
messages.body_plain:
My workplace has finally whitelisted google, so now I can participate
much more easily in this group.  If it is of any use to members of
this group to know a little more about reading rhipe data outside of
hadoop, here is a recent exchange that should have taken place here on
the group:

On 10/24/11 12:04 PM, "Saptarshi Guha"  wrote:

Yes, map files are sequence files + index file (wich is a small subset
of of the sorted keys)

On Mon, Oct 24, 2011 at 12:04 PM, Hafen, Ryan  wrote:

I see.  Ultimately we will be reading these in Java so this is good -
I
was just testing in Python since that's easier :).  Is the same true
for
map files?

On 10/24/11 11:54 AM, "Saptarshi Guha"  wrote:

My bad. I misinterpreted the code. the integer lengths are sent to the
RHIPE server to write to a sequence file.
rhwrite writes objects as sequence files. These are hadoop files of
k-value pairs and can be read in Java and Java only.

To read from Java, see
http://code.google.com/p/rhipe/source/browse/code/java/org/godhuli/rhipe/R
HReader.java

The interesting is stuff is in 61-64.

So this raises two issues that i've encountered before

1. Sequence files are java specific (Hadoop Java) and can't be read
from other lamnguages
2. You can manually convert the Sequence files to integer-length,
serialized object types using a specific fileformat (but it wont be
splittable) - the FileOutputFormat wiould need to just write integer
length and serialized objetcs.

3. AVRO have their own file format (similar to Sequence Files). I
should or someone should prepapare a RHIPE protobuf file format that
can be read from other languages.

On Mon, Oct 24, 2011 at 11:43 AM, Hafen, Ryan
wrote:

Good to know about the first part being an integer.

Preceding the integer there is the text "SEQ" (indicating a sequence
file?) and following the integer there is also the text:
"!org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable!org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable"
which I also removed.  After that is removed I still get the same
error.
Perhaps I am using the wrong .proto file?  I've attached the
rexp.proto
I
am using, which I got from the Rhipe 0.65.2 documentation.  I'm using
Rhipe 0.66.

I am using protocol buffers v2.4.1 and python v2.6.1.  Does your
"protoc
-I=. --python_out=. rexp.proto" successfully run and create a
rexp_pb2.pyc and rexp_pb2.py?

On 10/23/11 7:22 PM, "Saptarshi Guha"  wrote:

Okay, for some reason my

import rexp_pb2

throws this
[GCC 4.5.2] on linux2
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
import rexp_pb2
Traceback (most recent call last):
 File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
 File "rexp_pb2.py", line 259, in <module>
   DESCRIPTOR.message_types_by_name['REXP'] = _REXP
AttributeError: 'FileDescriptor' object has no attribute
'message_types_by_name'

But, rhwrite does this
For every object:
1. write length of the serialized object, big endian
2. write the object

So you should first read an integer in big endian format, then read
that many bytes and then deserialize this read object.

Hope it helps.

On Fri, Oct 21, 2011 at 11:28 AM, Hafen, Ryan
wrote:

One of my projects wants to concurrently use data used for RHIPE
analysis
for a java application.  We have been evaluating how it works to read
data
into java (and python too) from RHIPE output from the HDFS.  Here's
the
test I am trying:

1. In R, write create a dummy data set:

dat <- list(k="a", v=c(1:10))
rhwrite(dat, "/tmp/testdat")

2. Copy to local file system: hadoop fs -copyToLocal /tmp/testdat/0
testdat

3. Now try to read it in to python:

3.1. Make sure you have installed the google protocol buffer python
module (located in protobuf-2.4.1/python)

3.2. Using the .proto file from RHIPE, create python module:

protoc -I=. --python_out=. rexp.proto

3.3. In python, try to read the file:

import rexp_pb2

rexp=rexp_pb2.REXP()
f = open("testdat", "rb")
rexp.ParseFromString(f.read())

I get the error: Tag had invalid wire type.

This is the same error the java people are getting.  If you think it's
completely a protocol buffers problem, that's fine and I'll sort it
out.
If, however, you see something in my process of getting the data from
RHIPE and from the HDFS that is not right, I'd appreciate any insight.

Thanks,

Ryan

So in R, and correct me if i'm wrong, the warning and error functions
are sent through
Re_WriteConsoleEx . So i can't differentiate a warning from an error.

Now the Java code receives this and throws an exception to kill the job.

My plan is this: for a debug mode

1. Errors return the map.input.file and block which has been sent to them.
2. These are are stored in a separate file.
3. RHIPE functions (say in R console) to read these blocks (in a
stream) for local in console debugging.
4. Optionally, during other uses, skip first N errors.

Does it sound okay?
Regards

I was curious if any other users could share what size of data they
have used Rhipe with and how their experience has been.

I am currently working with 2 TB of data, which is stored as 16K
sequence files at ~128 MB each.

When I run a job with this data as the input, it takes about 12-15
minutes just to set up the job with rhmr, with something like z <-
rhmr(..., ifolder="/inputdata/p*").  I am guessing that this is
because it needs to get a listing of all these files?  Just checking
to see if this is normal behavior that others are experiencing or if I
should look into doing something about it.

messages.subject: Orderby="Integer" in Rhipe MapReduce
messages.subject_clean: Orderby="Integer" in Rhipe MapReduce
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm new to R and Rhipe ... so please excuse my ignorance here.  Trying
to learn a couple new things at once and its slow going.  I'm having
trouble ordering a list of integers in a data.frame.  Just so we can
have  common frame of reference, I've put my question below in terms
of the Arline Dataset example contained with the 65.2 Documentation.
I want to get a result set back that is ordered by the 'dist' column.
Here is the original script:

setup <- expression({
  convertHHMM <- function(s){
    t(sapply(s,function(r){
      l=nchar(r)
      if(l==4) c(substr(r,1,2),substr(r,3,4))
      else if(l==3) c(substr(r,1,1),substr(r,2,3))
      else c('0','0')
    })
  )}
})
map <- expression({
  y <- do.call("rbind",lapply(map.values,function(r){
    if(substr(r,1,4)!='Year') strsplit(r,",")[[1]]
  }))
  mu <- rep(1,nrow(y));yr <- y[,1]; mn=y[,2];dy=y[,3]
  hr <- convertHHMM(y[,5])
  depart <- ISOdatetime(year=yr,month=mn,day=dy,hour=hr[,1],min=hr[,
2],sec=mu)
  hr <- convertHHMM(y[,6])
  sdepart <- ISOdatetime(year=yr,month=mn,day=dy,hour=hr[,1],min=hr[,
2],sec=mu)
  hr <- convertHHMM(y[,7])
  arrive <- ISOdatetime(year=yr,month=mn,day=dy,hour=hr[,1],min=hr[,
2],sec=mu)
  hr <- convertHHMM(y[,8])
  sarrive <- ISOdatetime(year=yr,month=mn,day=dy,hour=hr[,1],min=hr[,
2],sec=mu)
  d <- data.frame(depart= depart,sdepart = sdepart
                ,arrive = arrive,sarrive =sarrive
                ,carrier = y[,9],origin = y[,17]
                ,dest=y[,18],dist = y[,19], year=yr, month-mn, day=dy
                ,cancelled=y[,22], stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  d <- d[order(d$sdepart),]
  rhcollect(d[c(1,nrow(d)),"sdepart"],d)
})
reduce <- expression(
    reduce = {
      lapply(reduce.values,function(i)
             rhcollect(reduce.key,i))}
    )
mapred <- list(rhipe_map_buff_size=5000)
z <- rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce,setup=setup,inout=c("text","sequence")
          ,ifolder="/airline/data/",ofolder="/airline/
blocks",mapred=mapred,orderby="numeric")
rhex(z)

I made the following mods to three lines of that MapReduce job based
on my research for ordering by the distance traveled ("dist" field):

  d <- d[order(d$dest),]

 rhcollect(d[c(1,nrow(d)),"dest"],d)

 z <-
rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce,setup=setup,inout=c("text","sequence")
          ,ifolder="/airline/data/",ofolder="/airline/
blocks",mapred=mapred,orderby="integer")

However, this doesn't work.  The dataset I get back isn't ordered by
"dist" in ascending or descending order.  Notice that there are quotes
around every field, to include all values in the 'dist' column.  That
indicates to me that R interprets each entry in the data.frame as a
string.  Perhaps that's why it's not sorting appropriately?  Would
greatly appreciate any help.

Thanks in advance,
Jeremy
